results.title: Live: Tripoli demands explanation from Kyiv for striking Russian ships in Libyan waters
results.content: The Tripoli-based Libyan foreign ministry on Monday condemned a Ukrainian drone attack on two Russian ships near the eastern city of Benghazi over the weekend, demanding an explanation from Kyiv. Meanwhile, South Korean authorities said Tuesday several Russian military aircraft had breached its air defence zone, correcting an earlier alert that reported a North Korean plane had made an incursion. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.

results.title: Jensen Huang's surprise return to Nvidia sparks mixed reactions in Washington
results.content: US President Donald Trump praised Nvidia's decision Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, as Democratic leaders vowed investigations and prominent Republicans questioned whether his return posed a national security risk.

results.title: US flew surveillance drone over Mexico to help capture top drug lord
results.content: Mexican officials say the United States flew a surveillance drone over Mexican territory to help locate and capture one of the country's most wanted drug traffickers. The operation led to the arrest of Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro'.

results.title: Zelensky urges four-way peace talks with Russia, Europe and US 'as soon as possible'
results.content: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is calling for a new round of negotiations involving Ukraine, Russia, the United States and European leaders, saying Kyiv is ready to meet as early as Tuesday.

results.title: 14 countries acknowledge ICJ ruling of genocide against Rohingya
results.content: Fourteen countries from Europe, Africa and Oceania have acknowledged a landmark ruling by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, calling on the country to comply with its obligations under international law. The United Kingdom separately announced sanctions against five senior Myanmar military figures and said it would formally recognise the genocide.

results.title: NATO vows space defence after Russia nuclear satellite report
results.content: NATO chief Mark Rutte said Monday the alliance would defend against threats in space when asked about German media reports that Russia may be preparing to launch a nuclear-armed satellite. The media reports, citing unnamed German military and BND spy agency sources, said Moscow was thought to be planning such a launch in the coming weeks, giving it the capability to destroy other satellites. FRANCE 24's Laurent Berstecher reports.

results.title: Africa disappointed with COP31 outcome
results.content: In tonight's edition, the COP31 climate summit in Turkey has failed to reach an agreement, exposing deep divisions over fossil fuels and climate finance. Also, DR Congo's Félix Tshisekedi and Kenya's William Ruto agree to restore relations and boost regional cooperation. And determined to help their children, parents in a South African township have transformed a discarded shipping container into a sensory room.

results.title: Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO
results.content: In a stunning U-turn, Nvidia's board has reinstated Jensen Huang as the company's President and CEO. The announcement came just days after the board rejected a petition calling for the tech titan's return. US President Donald Trump said had personally got in touch with the board to advocate for his return. Nvidia's stock surged 32%, adding nearly $1 trillion to its market cap while the rest of Wall Street also rallied.

results.title: 'A war of unmanned machines, AI and total transparency of the battlefield'
results.content: Speaking with FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney, Nobel Peace Prize laureate Oleksandra Matviichuk, Director of the Centre for Civil Liberties, says that today's war in Ukraine "is a war of unmanned machines, AI, total transparency of the battlefield, mass drones attacks and long range weapons, and this means we have to rethink how to protect human beings".

results.title: Libya's east seeks UN probe into claims Ukrainian military present in west
results.content: Authorities in divided Libya's east called on Monday for the United Nations to investigate claims that Ukrainian forces were present in the country's west, as they lodged a complaint over Ukrainian attacks on two Russian ships off Benghazi. The strikes on Sunday, claimed by Kyiv, come as Ukraine steps up strikes against Russia far from the front lines of their war. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

results.title: Trump backs Nvidia boss's return but top Democrat vows probe
results.content: US President Donald Trump praised Nvidia's decision Monday to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive, as top Senate Democrat Chuck Schumer vowed to investigate potential wrongdoing amid mounting national security concerns. Trump also posted a doctored version of the famous photograph of him raising his fist after surviving a 2024 assassination attempt, replacing himself with Huang, who brandished a red bra beneath an Nvidia flag. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson reports from Washington.

results.title: How far will Ukraine war spread? Kyiv targets Russian vessels in Libya
results.content: Talk about spillover. In the Libyan port of Benghazi, Ukraine claiming responsibility for the sinkings first of a Russian warship and then a cargo vessel. That’s on top of the sanctioned ship struck in the Baltic Sea that’s since strayed into Finland’s waters. Legitimate targets?

results.title: Ukraine claims it sank Russian warship off Libya
results.content: Ukraine on Monday claimed it was behind strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya, including one that sank a modern warship, in the latest spillover from Moscow's invasion. The attacks on Sunday near the Libyan port of Benghazi come at a time when Ukraine has stepped up its daring strikes against Russia far from the frontlines in retaliation for Moscow's deadly invasion. FRANCE 24's Gulliver Cragg reports from Kyiv.

results.title: Nvidia reinstates Huang as CEO after Trump intervention
results.content: Nvidia on Monday reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive in a stunning reversal that President Donald Trump said followed his own direct contacts with the company's board. Huang resigned two weeks ago over an affair with a woman whom US intelligence agencies suspect of spying for China, a departure that sent Wall Street tumbling and stoked fears for a US economy reliant on the AI investment boom. FRANCE 24's Carys Garland and Wassim Cornet report.

results.title: 'Maintain control': UN chief calls for creation of global AI safety framework within a year
results.content: UN chief Antonio Guterres on Monday urged countries to agree on the creation of a global framework for managing the dangers posed by artificial intelligence within one year. Speaking at a summit in Barbados, he warned that taming the technology is vital if humanity is to stay in charge of its own future.

results.title: 'Deeply shocked': Gisèle Pelicot to sue publisher after nude photos used in book campaign
results.content: French feminist icon Gisèle Pelicot, who became a worldwide symbol against sexual violence during the 2024 rape trials against her husband and dozens of other men, said Monday she will take legal action after nude images of her were sent out without her permission to publicise a psychoanalyst's book on coercive control.

results.title: Finland summons Russian ambassador after suspected airspace violation
results.content: Finland on Monday said it had summoned Russia's ambassador over a suspected violation of Finnish airspace by a Russian helicopter and after a Ukrainian drone strike on a Russian cargo ship located in the Gulf of Finland in recent days. Helsinki also condemned Moscow's escalating strikes on civilian targets in Ukraine.

Airports, public transport shut down amid national strike in Belgium
results.content: Belgium's prime minister on Monday set a new year-end deadline for his coalition government to agree a cost-cutting budget or face collapse. The announcement came as a national strike against the planned cuts grounded all flights in and out of Belgium. Public transport, schools and other public services also faced disruption. France 24's Dave Keating has the latest from Brussels.

results.title: Iran's courts order US to pay $290 billion in damages
results.content: Iranian courts have ordered the United States to pay $290 billion in damages for decades of US actions against the Islamic Republic, a judiciary official said Monday. He added that lawsuits have also been filed against Gulf Arab states accused of letting Washington use their territory to strike Iran.

results.title: 12,000 evacuated from Don Toliver concert after unknown substance sickens fans
results.content: More than 12,000 fans were evacuated from a concert by American rapper Don Toliver and over 80 were treated by medics after an unknown irritant was released in the crowd, authorities in the English city of Manchester said Monday.

results.title: Behind COP31 failure: A showdown over fossil fuel interests
results.content: Several countries and environmental groups expressed fury at the collapse of the COP31 climate conference in Antalya, Turkey on Sunday, amid a dramatic failure to thrash out an agreement, two days after the summit was scheduled to end. Oil-producing states blocked any mention of phasing out fossil fuels – the root cause of the climate crisis – with the EU then refusing to back a weakened text. Our Environment Editor Valerie Dekimpe tells us more.

results.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
results.content: Nvidia said on Monday it was reinstating Jensen Huang as ​CEO, effective immediately, an extraordinary reversal that followed calls from US President Donald Trump for his return after Huang resigned over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman alleged to have spied for China. France 24's Fraser Jackson has the details.
